subproblem.title: Reference smooth approximations near a closed set: C^∞, derivative bound Λ on the r/2-neighbourhood, uniform convergence and eventual properness (supplied Step 2)
subproblem.statement: Notation: ℝ^p := Eucl p; A_ρ := thickening ρ A; C^∞ means ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞); a map g is proper on F if g⁻¹(K) ∩ F is compact for every compact K. Let (SA) be the following proposition (it is verbatim the frozen statement of the sibling node smooth_approx, Lean name dph_lipschitz_smooth_approx, of the parent pushforward_homotopy): for all m, m′ ∈ ℕ, G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0, A ⊆ ℝ^m and δ ∈ ℝ with δ > 0 and G Λ-Lipschitz on A_δ: there are Ĝ : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, maps G_j : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} (j ∈ ℕ) and L ∈ ℝ≥0 such that: (a) Ĝ is L-Lipschitz on ℝ^m and Ĝ = G on thickening δ A; (b) every G_j is C^∞ (ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞)) and L-Lipschitz on ℝ^m; (c) G_j → Ĝ uniformly on ℝ^m; (d) ‖fderiv ℝ G_j x‖ ≤ Λ for all j and all x ∈ thickening (δ/2) A; (e) (tangential vanishing) for all k ∈ ℕ, α ∈ SimonMultiIndex k m′, z ∈ ℝ^{m′}, ω ∈ TestFormOn univ k (on ℝ^{m′}) and ε > 0 such that every x ∈ thickening ε A with G(x) ∈ thickening ε (tsupport ω) satisfies G(x)_i = z_i for every i ∉ range α, and ω(y)(e_{α(1)}, …, e_{α(k)}) = 0 for every y ∈ ℝ^{m′} (e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1), there is r > 0 such that for all sufficiently large j and all x ∈ thickening r A the covector ω(G_j(x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ G_j x) is zero. Claim: if (SA) holds, then for all m, m′ ∈ ℕ, G : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′}, Λ ∈ ℝ≥0, r ∈ ℝ and F ⊆ ℝ^m such that r > 0, F is closed, G is Λ-Lipschitz on F_r and G is proper on F, there are C^∞ maps G_n : ℝ^m → ℝ^{m′} (n ∈ ℕ) with ‖fderiv ℝ G_n x‖ ≤ Λ for all n and all x ∈ F_{r/2}, G_n → G uniformly on F_{r/2}, and G_n proper on F for all sufficiently large n.
subproblem.lean_statement: (∀ (m m' : ℕ) (G : Eucl m → Eucl m') (Λ : ℝ≥0) (A : Set (Eucl m)) (δ : ℝ), 0 < δ → LipschitzOnWith Λ G (thickening δ A) → ∃ (G' : Eucl m → Eucl m') (Gj : ℕ → Eucl m → Eucl m') (L : ℝ≥0), LipschitzWith L G' ∧ EqOn G' G (thickening δ A) ∧ (∀ j, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) (Gj j)) ∧ (∀ j, LipschitzWith L (Gj j)) ∧ TendstoUniformly Gj G' atTop ∧ (∀ j, ∀ x ∈ thickening (δ / 2) A, ‖fderiv ℝ (Gj j) x‖ ≤ Λ) ∧ ∀ (k : ℕ) (α : SimonMultiIndex k m') (z : Eucl m') (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Eucl m')) k) (ε : ℝ), 0 < ε → (∀ x ∈ thickening ε A, G x ∈ thickening ε (tsupport (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl m') k)) → ∀ i, i ∉ range α → G x i = z i) → (∀ y, (ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl m') k) y (fun j => EuclideanSpace.single (α j) (1 : ℝ)) = 0) → ∃ r : ℝ, 0 < r ∧ ∀ᶠ j in atTop, ∀ x ∈ thickening r A, ((ω : DifferentialForm (Eucl m') k) (Gj j x)).compContinuousLinearMap (fderiv ℝ (Gj j) x) = 0) → (∀ (m m' : ℕ) (G : Eucl m → Eucl m') (Λ : ℝ≥0) (r : ℝ) (F : Set (Eucl m)), 0 < r → IsClosed F → LipschitzOnWith Λ G (thickening r F) → (∀ K : Set (Eucl m'), IsCompact K → IsCompact (G ⁻¹' K ∩ F)) → ∃ Gj : ℕ → Eucl m → Eucl m', (∀ n, ContDiff ℝ ((⊤ : ℕ∞) : WithTop ℕ∞) (Gj n)) ∧ (∀ n, ∀ x ∈ thickening (r / 2) F, ‖fderiv ℝ (Gj n) x‖ ≤ Λ) ∧ TendstoUniformlyOn Gj G atTop (thickening (r / 2) F) ∧ ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ K : Set (Eucl m'), IsCompact K → IsCompact (Gj n ⁻¹' K ∩ F))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Step 2 of the supplied proof of lipschitz_pushforward (reference sequence), stated for an arbitrary closed set F (Step 2 uses F = spt X, Step 8 uses F = spt X ∪ spt X₁). Assume (SA) and fix m, m′, G, Λ, r, F as in the claim.

1. (Apply (SA).) Apply (SA) with A := F and δ := r (r > 0 and G is Λ-Lipschitz on F_r). It gives Ĝ, maps G_n and L with: Ĝ = G on F_r (part (a)); every G_n is C^∞ (part (b)); G_n → Ĝ uniformly on ℝ^m (part (c)); ‖fderiv ℝ G_n x‖ ≤ Λ for every n and every x ∈ F_{r/2} (part (d)). Part (e) and the Lipschitz constant L are not used. Smoothness and the derivative bound are two of the three required properties.
2. (Uniform convergence to G on F_{r/2}.) Since 0 < r/2 ≤ r, F_{r/2} ⊆ F_r (thickening_mono), so Ĝ = G on F_{r/2}. Uniform convergence on ℝ^m implies uniform convergence on the subset F_{r/2} (TendstoUniformly.tendstoUniformlyOn), and since the limit Ĝ agrees with G on F_{r/2}, G_n → G uniformly on F_{r/2} (TendstoUniformlyOn.congr_right).
3. (Eventual closeness on F.) F ⊆ F_{r/2} because r/2 > 0 (self_subset_thickening). By step 2 and the metric characterization of uniform convergence (Metric.tendstoUniformlyOn_iff) with ε = 1, there is n₀ such that for all n ≥ n₀ and all x ∈ F_{r/2}, dist(G(x), G_n(x)) < 1; in particular dist(G_n(x), G(x)) ≤ 1 for all n ≥ n₀ and x ∈ F.
4. (Eventual properness.) Let n ≥ n₀. G_n is continuous (a C^∞ map is continuous), F is closed, G is proper on F and dist(G_n(x), G(x)) ≤ 1 on F, so part (a) of the sibling proper_transfer (with g := G_n and d := 1) shows that G_n is proper on F. Hence G_n is proper on F for all sufficiently large n, which completes the proof. ∎
proof_key_steps: Apply (SA) with A := F, δ := r: C^∞ maps G_n, ‖DG_n‖ ≤ Λ on F_{r/2}, G_n → Ĝ uniformly with Ĝ = G on F_r.
Restrict the uniform convergence to F_{r/2} ⊆ F_r and replace Ĝ by G there (congr_right).
Eventually dist(G_n, G) ≤ 1 on F ⊆ F_{r/2}; proper_transfer (a) makes G_n proper on F.
